guidance: Always drink clean, treated water. Boil water for at least 1 minute (at high altitudes, boil for 3 minutes) or use certified water purification methods (filter, chlorinate, or UV). Store drinking water in clean, covered containers. Use a clean ladle to draw water.
precautions: Store drinking water in covered containers
Do not use contaminated sources
Clean water storage containers weekly
Avoid dipping hands or cups into stored water
If unsure, treat water before drinking

category: Water Source Protection – Wells and Borewells
guidance: Protect wells and borewells from surface contamination. Ensure proper lining and a concrete apron. Keep the area clean, avoid stagnant water nearby, and test water quality periodically. Cover the well to prevent debris and animals from entering.
precautions: Keep wells at least 15 metres from latrines
Construct a raised platform with drainage
Do not allow animals near the well
Test for coliform bacteria regularly
Chlorinate if contamination is detected

guidance: Store water in narrow‑necked, clean, covered containers. Use a tap or ladle to draw water. Clean containers weekly with soap and water, and allow to dry in the sun. Keep storage away from animals and waste.
precautions: Do not store water in open containers
Clean containers regularly with bleach solution
Do not touch water with hands – use a ladle
Keep water containers off the floor
If water is untreated, treat before storage

guidance: Boiling is the most reliable way to kill pathogens. Bring water to a rolling boil and keep it there for at least 1 minute (3 minutes at altitudes >2000m). Allow to cool in the same container, covered. Boiled water can be stored for 24 hours in a clean covered container.
precautions: Do not overboil – wastes fuel
Use boiled water within 24 hours
Store boiled water in a clean container
If water is cloudy, filter before boiling

guidance: Use chlorine tablets or liquid bleach (sodium hypochlorite) to disinfect water. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for dosage – typically 1–2 drops of 1% bleach per litre of clear water, or 2–4 drops for cloudy water. Wait 30 minutes before drinking. A slight chlorine smell indicates adequate disinfection.
precautions: Do not use scented or colour‑safe bleach
Store chlorine tablets in a cool, dark place
If water has a strong chlorine smell, let it stand for a few hours
Do not over‑chlorinate – can cause gastrointestinal irritation
Test chlorine residual if possible (0.2–0.5 mg/L is safe)

guidance: Ceramic filters, biosand filters, and gravity filters remove bacteria, protozoa, and suspended particles. Clean the filter regularly as per manufacturer instructions. Biosand filters require a slow flow rate – do not rush water through. Replace filter cartridges when needed.
precautions: Do not use filters that are cracked or damaged
Clean the filter surface regularly
Do not use with water that is heavily turbid – pre‑settle or pre‑filter
Follow maintenance schedule
If filter is new, run a few litres of water through and discard

guidance: Fill clear PET plastic bottles with water, shake to aerate, and place in direct sunlight for 6 hours (or 2 days if cloudy). The UV rays kill pathogens. Suitable for small quantities. Do not use bottles that are scratched or old. After treatment, store away from light.
precautions: Use clear, colourless PET bottles (not glass)
Do not use bottles larger than 2 litres
If water is turbid, filter first
Do not drink water that has been in sunlight for more than 2 days
SODIS does not remove chemicals – only biological contaminants

guidance: The most effective approach is to use multiple barriers: pre‑settlement (let water stand to settle sediment), filtration, and then disinfection (chlorine, UV, or boiling). This ensures safe drinking water even from questionable sources.
precautions: Do not rely on a single method if water quality is poor
Combine physical and chemical treatment for best results
Store treated water safely
Monitor water quality visually (clarity, odour)
If in doubt, boil the water

guidance: Wash hands with soap and clean water for at least 20 seconds: before eating, after using the toilet, after handling waste, after coughing/sneezing, before and after caring for a sick person, and before preparing food. Scrub all surfaces (palms, backs, between fingers, under nails).
precautions: Use soap (or ash if soap is unavailable)
Rinse well with clean running water
Dry hands with a clean cloth or air dry
If water is scarce, use alcohol‑based hand sanitiser (≥60% alcohol)
Teach children proper handwashing technique

category: Handwashing Facilities in Schools and Communities
guidance: Install handwashing stations with soap and water at schools, health centres, and public places. Ensure they are accessible to all (including children and people with disabilities). Provide regular maintenance and soap refills. Promote handwashing through school hygiene clubs.
precautions: Ensure soap is always available
Provide a water source (tap or bucket with a tap)
Build stations at a height accessible to children
Place near toilets and eating areas
Conduct regular hygiene promotion sessions

guidance: Use sanitary toilets (flush, pour‑flush, pit latrines, or composting toilets) to prevent open defecation. Keep them clean and well‑maintained. Regularly empty pits safely, and ensure handwashing facilities are nearby.

Clean the toilet daily with disinfectant

category: Open Defecation – Health and Social Risks
symptoms: increased risk of diarrhoea, worm infections, and environmental contamination
guidance: Open defecation spreads diseases (cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A, helminths) and affects community dignity. Use a toilet every time. If toilets are not available, build a simple pit latrine. Community education and motivation are key to ending open defecation.
precautions: Do not defecate in open – it contaminates water sources

If you have no toilet, build a temporary pit with a cover
Wash hands thoroughly after defecation
Participate in community sanitation drives

category: Safe Disposal of Human Faeces (For Rural Areas)
guidance: Faeces should be contained in a pit latrine or septic tank. If no toilet, use a shallow pit (1–2 metres deep) that is covered after each use. When the pit is nearly full, fill with soil and mark it. Do not use faeces as fertiliser without proper composting. Ensure pits are at least 30 metres from water sources.
precautions: Keep toilet pits away from wells
Do not allow children to play near pits
Cover pit after use to prevent fly breeding
Empty pits only by trained personnel
Use protective gear when handling faeces

guidance: Septic tanks should be desludged every 2–5 years by a licensed operator. Do not put grease, chemicals, or non‑biodegradable items down the drain. Ensure soak pits are functioning and not blocked. Check for leaks and odours.
precautions: Do not dispose of cooking oil or solvents into the septic tank
Use biodegradable toilet paper
Do not park vehicles over the tank
Keep the manhole cover secure
If you smell gas, ventilate and call a professional

category: Food Safety – Storage, Preparation, and Handling
symptoms: food poisoning, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal cramps
guidance: Keep raw and cooked foods separate. Store perishable foods in a cool place (below 5°C if possible). Cook food thoroughly (internal temperature >70°C). Reheat leftovers to at least 75°C. Avoid keeping cooked food at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

Use separate chopping boards for raw meat and vegetables
Do not thaw food at room temperature – use a refrigerator or cold water
Cover food to protect from flies and dust

guidance: Wash fruits and vegetables under clean running water before eating or cooking. For root vegetables, scrub with a brush. For leafy greens, soak in clean water for a few minutes and rinse. Do not use soap or detergent on produce. Peel fruits if skin is damaged.

If water is unsafe, use boiled or chlorinated water
Remove outer leaves of leafy vegetables
Use a clean brush for scrubbing

guidance: Store dry foods (grains, pulses) in airtight containers in a cool, dry place. Keep them off the floor and away from pests. Store perishables in a refrigerator (if available) or a cool, dark, ventilated place. Check for signs of spoilage.

Cover food to protect from flies and rodents
Use older food first (first‑in, first‑out)

guidance: Clean kitchen surfaces with soap and water, then disinfect with a diluted bleach solution (1 tablespoon bleach in 1 litre water). Wash dishes with hot water and detergent, and allow to air dry. Change dishcloths and sponges regularly.

Use separate cutting boards for meat and vegetables

guidance: Separate waste into biodegradable (kitchen waste, garden waste) and non‑biodegradable (plastics, glass, metal). Compost biodegradable waste in a covered bin. Dispose of non‑biodegradable waste in designated collection points. Reduce, reuse, and recycle.

guidance: Compost kitchen scraps, garden waste, and manure in a bin or pit. Mix with dry leaves and soil. Turn regularly to aerate. Keep the compost moist but not wet. It should be ready in 2–3 months. Use finished compost as fertiliser.

Do not use fresh manure – must be fully composted

guidance: Reduce plastic use – carry reusable bags, bottles, and containers. Avoid single‑use plastics. Recycle plastic waste through local collection systems. Never burn plastic. Participate in clean‑up drives.
precautions: Do not litter plastic in the environment

Do not use plastic for storing hot food (leaches chemicals)

precautions: Do not throw garbage in public spaces

If you see a blocked drain, report it

Use fly swatters or sticky traps

Use non‑toxic methods if possible

symptoms: skin infections, body odour, fungal infections
guidance: Bathe daily with soap and water. Wash your hair regularly. Wear clean clothes and change underwear daily. Keep nails short and clean. Use a clean towel and do not share personal items. Good hygiene prevents skin and respiratory infections.

If you have a skin infection, avoid scratching
Use soap that does not irritate your skin

Do not share nail clippers
If you have athlete's foot, treat it promptly
Use moisturiser on dry feet (but not between toes)

symptoms: dental caries, gum disease, bad breath

Do not use excessive pressure when brushing

guidance: Change sanitary pads/tampons every 4–6 hours. Wash hands before and after changing. Dispose of used pads in a bin (do not flush). Use clean cloth pads and wash them with soap, rinse, and dry in sunlight. Menstrual cups are eco‑friendly – clean with soap and boil between cycles.

Seek professional testing for chemical contaminants (fluoride, arsenic)

Follow local health department advice

category: Arsenic in Drinking Water – Health Risks
guidance: If your water has high arsenic (>10 µg/L), use alternative sources (deep wells, rainwater) or install arsenic removal filters (oxidation, co‑precipitation, reverse osmosis). Long‑term exposure is harmful. Government provides testing and mitigation in affected areas.

Monitor arsenic levels regularly
Educate community about risks

guidance: Iron and manganese are generally not harmful to health but can affect taste and appearance. Use oxidation filters or ion exchange to remove. Let water settle and use the clear portion. If high levels, consult a water treatment specialist.

Collect rainwater for drinking
Use a water softener if needed

guidance: Collect rainwater from clean roofs into storage tanks. Fit gutters and filters to remove debris. First‑flush diverters remove the initial contaminated water. Store in covered tanks. Treat water (boil, chlorinate, or filter) before drinking. Rainwater is soft and safe if properly managed.

Use a first‑flush diverter
Store water in clean, covered tanks

Clean the tank regularly

Monitor water levels
Participate in watershed management programs

guidance: After floods, assume all water is contaminated. Drink only bottled or boiled water. Use ORS for diarrhoea. Clean houses and utensils with bleach. Drain stagnant water. Boil water for 3 minutes. Wash hands frequently. Seek medical care for fever or diarrhoea.

Boil drinking water

If you have water, share it with neighbours
Use efficient irrigation
Monitor water quality during scarcity

Provide cups or water fountains

guidance: Street vendors should use clean water, wash hands frequently, keep food covered, and avoid touching food with bare hands. Encourage vendors to use gloves and utensils. Consumers should choose vendors who practice good hygiene.

Watch for cleanliness of vendor
If possible, choose cooked hot food
Avoid raw salads from street vendors
Support vendor hygiene training

guidance: Restaurants and food stalls must have handwashing facilities with soap and water. Staff should wash hands before and after handling food, after using the toilet, and after handling raw meat. Display handwashing reminders.

Provide hand drying facilities
Train staff in food hygiene
Monitor compliance

guidance: Soak vegetables in water with a few crystals of potassium permanganate (to a light pink colour) for 15 minutes, then rinse thoroughly with clean water. This helps remove pesticide residues and bacteria. Use caution – do not make the water too dark.

Do not use with all vegetables – test on a small batch
Rinse well after soaking
Keep potassium permanganate out of children's reach

guidance: Soak vegetables in salt water (1 tablespoon salt per litre) for 10–15 minutes, then rinse with clean water. This can help remove dirt and some pesticides. Not a substitute for thorough washing. Use for leafy greens and fruits.

Rinse thoroughly after soaking
Do not use salt water for prolonged soaking
Use only if water is safe
Combine with regular washing

guidance: Plant lemongrass, citronella, neem, tulsi, marigold, and basil around homes to repel mosquitoes and other insects. Crush leaves to release repellent oils. This is a natural and eco‑friendly approach.

Keep plants trimmed
Use neem oil as a natural pesticide
If you have allergies, test a small area

category: Use of Mosquito Nets – Proper Installation
guidance: Install insecticide‑treated mosquito nets (ITNs) over beds. Tuck edges under the mattress. Ensure there are no holes. Retreat nets with insecticide as recommended. Use nets all year round, especially during rainy season.
precautions: Do not wash ITNs with soap (may wash away insecticide)
If nets have holes, repair them
Use nets even during the day for young children
If you are pregnant, use a net
Replace nets every 2–3 years

category: Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS) – What to Expect
guidance: IRS involves spraying insecticide on the inside walls of houses to kill mosquitoes. It is safe when done by trained personnel. Leave the house during spraying and for a few hours after. Do not wipe off the insecticide – it remains effective for months.
precautions: Do not stay indoors during spraying
Cover food and water sources
Do not clean the walls for at least 2 weeks
If you have allergies, inform the spray team
Support IRS campaigns

guidance: Organise regular clean‑up drives to clear trash, remove stagnant water, and clean drains. Involve all community members. Use the 'Swachh Bharat' framework. Provide gloves and masks. Dispose of collected waste properly.

Do not touch hazardous waste
Segregate waste during collection
Promote the event in advance

category: Safe Handling of Drinking Water in Public Places
guidance: In public places (train stations, bus stops), provide clean water points with proper drainage. Ensure taps are clean and functional. Use signage to encourage safe water practices. Regular maintenance is essential.

Monitor water quality regularly
If contamination is found, close the source

category: Water and Sanitation in Slums – Special Focus
guidance: Slums often lack basic WASH services. Advocate for piped water, sewers, and toilets. Community partnerships with local government are key. Use low‑cost solutions (community toilets, water kiosks). Involve residents in planning.

Monitor for disease outbreaks

category: Water Testing Kits – Use and Interpretation
guidance: Use simple water testing kits for chlorine residual, pH, turbidity, and coliform bacteria. Follow instructions carefully. If coliform is detected, treat the water. Confirm with laboratory testing if possible.
precautions: Use fresh test strips
Read results according to the time specified
If you are unsure, repeat the test

category: Protecting Water Sources from Animal Contamination
guidance: Fence water sources (wells, springs, ponds) to keep animals away. Ensure proper drainage to prevent runoff from animal areas entering water. Provide separate water for livestock.

Keep water sources covered
If animals contaminate a source, disinfect it
Educate livestock owners
Monitor for faecal contamination

category: Safe Water for Infants – Formula Preparation
guidance: For infants under 6 months, use boiled and cooled water for formula. Boil water for 1 minute, cool to 70°C, then add formula (as per instructions). Do not use water from unsafe sources. Clean bottles and teats thoroughly.
precautions: Do not use untreated water for formula
Prepare formula just before feeding
Do not store prepared formula
Clean bottles with hot soapy water and sterilise
If safe water is unavailable, breastfeed exclusively

guidance: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission) aims to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management. It promotes toilet construction, behaviour change, and cleanliness. Participate in local Swachhata drives and use government‑built toilets.

guidance: Bleach (sodium hypochlorite) is effective for disinfecting surfaces, toilets, and water. Dilute as per instructions: for surfaces, 1:10 dilution; for water, 1–2 drops per litre (depending on concentration). Never mix bleach with acid or ammonia.
